value: For the declared binary M1 ancestor-first fixed-quota model, the complete finite generative PMF contains jointly independent named ancestor and leaf correctness bits and three independent primitive bits per member: ancestor selector, conditional leaf selector, and fresh vote. Summing unused primitive draws gives exclusive masses c1, (1-c1)c2, (1-c1)(1-c2)p and (1-c1)(1-c2)(1-p). Pushing this law to named lineage counts yields the product binomial law with q_l=c1 A_parent(l)+(1-c1)c2 B_l+(1-c1)(1-c2)p. For every finite N its fair-majority error is exactly the finite latent mixture of binomial errors. This identity is compiled in Lean without assuming a count law or convergence theorem. It does not prove an asymptotic floor, a CLT, a calibrated public API or causal identification.
